name: Summoner Holo-knight
body:
Traditionally the summoner is a conduit through which existences and powers from planes beyond the material can manifest in the world. The holo-knight however, uses technology and the abilities of a special suit of mechanical armor to wade into battle backed by dangerous “tricks of the light.”

Projectionist Savant

The holo-knight adds technomancy and all illusion spells from the sorcerer/wizard spell list to his summoner spell list.

This alters the summoner’s spells.

Bonded Mech

The holo-knight gains a bonded mech*, treating his class level as his pilot level.

This replaces eidolon, life link, maker’s call, life bond, and merge forms.

Hard Light Summons

Whenever the holo-knight uses his summon monster spell-like ability, any creatures he summons are partially real illusions rather than solid creations. The effect is considered an illusion spell rather than a conjuration spell. Creatures are allowed a Will save to recognize the summoned creatures as illusory as per the shadow conjuration spell. A shadow creature has one-fifth the hit points of a normal creature of its kind (regardless of whether it is recognized as shadowy). It deals normal damage and has all normal abilities and weaknesses.

Against a creature that recognizes it as a shadow creature, however, the shadow creature’s damage is one-fifth (20%) normal, and all special abilities that do not deal lethal damage are only 20% likely to work. (Roll for each use and each affected character separately.) Furthermore, the shadow creature’s AC bonuses are just one-fifth as large. A creature that succeeds at its save sees the shadow conjurations as transparent images superimposed on vague, shadowy forms. Objects automatically succeed at their Will saves against this spell.

This alters summon monster I.

Reinforced Images

At 2nd level, a holo-knight gains Solid Shadows as a bonus feat and may apply this metamagic feat to their summon monster spell-like ability without changing the ability’s level or casting time. The holo-knight does not need to meet the prerequisites for this feat.

This replaces bond senses.

Shield Emitters (Ex)

At 4th level, whenever the holo-knight is adjacent to or piloting their bonded mech, he gains a +2 shield bonus to their Armor Class and a +2 circumstance bonus on his saving throws.

This replaces shield ally.

Mobile Emitters (Su)

At 8th level the holo-knight no longer needs to be adjacent to or piloting their bonded mech to gain the benefits of the shield emitters ability. The holo-knight also gains the benefits of their shield emitter ability while adjacent to a creature summoned using their hard light summons ability.

This replaces transposition.

Virtual Upgrade (Su)

At 10th level holo-knight gains the ability to augment the functions of their bonded mech with holograms. The bonded mech gains a bonus Mech Enhancement that it qualifies for. The holo-knight may exchange this Mech Enhancement with any other that his bonded mech qualifies for with a minute of work.

A virtual upgrade does not count towards the number of Mech Enhancements the mech has for the purposes of deciding how long it takes to alter its body type, but can be changed during that process. A second virtual upgrade is gained at 18th level.

This ability replaces aspect and greater aspect.

Enhanced Shield Emitters (Su)

At 12th level, whenever the holo-knight is piloting his bonded mech, any ally within reach of their mech gains a +2 shield bonus to its Armor Class and a +2 circumstance bonus on its saving throws. In addition the bonuses granted by the holo-knights shield emitters ability increases to +4.

This replaces greater shield ally.
